content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper develops a self-supervised graph representation learning method. It doesn't rely on corruption techniques to augment the graph data. Experiments on small, medium, large-scale data show its effectiveness.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The strength of this paper is:
1) The motivation and writing are clear. 
2) Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. 
3) The proposed method saves memory usage. 
The weaknesses are:
1) The novelty is limited. There are several works using neighbors as positive/negative pairs. 
2) There are a number of augmentation-free methods in the literature. Therefore, it would be necessary to compare them. 
3) The performance on small and medium-size data is not significant.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Basically, this paper minimizes the distance between the learned similarity matrix and the diffusion matrix. The proposed method is simple and easy to implement. Though there are some typos, the writing is clear and easy to follow. My main concern is about the technical contribution of this paper. Similar to [1-2], it is still to mine the neighborhood information. The objective function in section 3.3 is also similar to [3], which uses the similarity to weight the neighbor.

[2] With a Little Help from My Friends: Nearest-Neighbor Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
[3] Graph-MLP: Node Classification without Message Passing in Graph

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes CURSIVE, a corruption-free single-view graph SSL approach. The core idea of CURSIVE is to construct positive samples with weights using diffusion, then contrastive learning can be performed naturally using the generated positive examples. Experimental results demonstrate that CURSIVE can outperforms existing SOTAs by a large margin while being more memory efficient.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. The motivation of this paper is good. Currently the most popuar self-supervised learning methods on graphs are following a multi-view perspective (either contrastive or non-contrasitve), where the multi-view data is generated from random data augmentations. Such a paradigm does lead to some limitations waiting to be addressed.
2. The intuition of using diffusion matrix as the reconstruction target is clear, reasonable and easy to understand.
3. The improvement over baseline methods is satisfying to me.

Weaknesses:
  1.  This paper has missed a lot of related works that also try to get rid of data augmentations and multi-view architectures in graph contrastive learning, e.g., [1] , [2], [3] . These papers resort to the graph stutures or other available useful information for creating self-supervised signals. The motivation and research task is closely related to this paper and should be definitly considered as realted works and baselines.
2. One important advantage claimed by this paper is its scalability. However, it is widely known that the computation of diffusion matrix is not scalable. I notice that the authors have used mini-batch training / Cluster-GCN to overcome the scalability issue, which enables the method to scale to large-scale graphs. However, I think these strageties could also be naturally applied to other methods, and there is no clear evidence that perform mini-batch training on the baseline methods does lead to sub-optimal performance. Also, it is unfair to perform scalabiltiy comparison when the proposed method uses mini-batch training while other methods use full-graph training.
3. The motivation of using graph diffusion should be the example in Fig. 1, where graph diffusion can help better discriminate clusters. However, I think not every graph dataset has such a clear cluster structure so that the graph diffusion can benefit. A more challenging case is heterophily graph, where connected nodes are likely have different labels. I guess that link-based contrastive objective should not work as well as augmentation-based ones in this case. 
4. I notice that the authors use a 3-layer GCN encoder for all approaches for fair comparison. However, according to my knowledege, most baselines uses a 2-layer GCN encoder by default. It might be unfair to compare their performance with different architectures (some times a deeper encoder is not better).

References:
[1] Namkyeong Lee, Junseok Lee, and Chanyoung Park. Augmentation-free self-supervised learning on graphs.
 arXiv preprint arXiv:2112.02472, 2021.
[2] Haonan Wang, Jieyu Zhang, Qi Zhu, and Wei Huang. Augmentation-free graph contrastive learning with performance guarantee. arXiv Preprint arXiv:2204.04874, 2022.
[3] Yujie Mo, Liang Peng, Jie Xu, Xiaoshuang Shi, and Xiaofeng Zhu. Simple unsupervised graph representation learning. In AAAI, pp. 7797–7805, 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed method is novel and clearly presented.
content.summary_of_the_review: Generally, I think the motivation of this paper is good, the proposed method is techinically reasonable and easy to follow, but can demonstate quite good performance. However, some previous papers have studied the same proposed their solutions while this paper just neglect all of them. Some contributions (e.g., scalability) are over-claimed, and I believe the application of the proposed method is limited. Due to these reasons, I would like to recommend a rejection.
